eatThis: Salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, anchovies — two portions a week moves you meaningfully toward supplement-range intakes, and the fish also brings vitamin D and, if you eat the bones, calcium
Note that flaxseed, chia and walnuts give ALA, which humans convert to EPA very inefficiently — they are good food, but not a route to a 1g EPA dose
avoidThis: DHA-predominant or 'balanced' fish oil products if depression is the target. In meta-regression, formulations that were pure EPA or EPA-major outperformed; DHA-predominant ones did not show the same benefit.

Assuming fish oil is definitely dangerous with an SSRI because both touch platelets. A 2024 JAHA meta-analysis of 15 randomised trials (120,643 patients) found no overall increase in bleeding with omega-3 supplements, and no signal that background antiplatelet therapy changed that. Two honest limits: those trials were cardiovascular trials that did not specifically study SSRI users, so this is reassuring rather than definitive for that pairing; and the same paper concluded that high-dose purified EPA (prescription icosapent ethyl, not a supplement) may carry a modest additional bleeding risk.
protocols.timeline: 8 weeks minimum before assessing; 8-12 weeks is where trial benefits appeared
protocols.source: Dosing: Guu et al., ISNPR practice guidelines, Psychother Psychosom 2019 — net EPA 1-2 g/day, EPA-pure or EPA-major, minimum 8 weeks, as adjunct. Formulation effect: Mocking et al., Transl Psychiatry 2016 meta-analysis and meta-regression — benefit concentrated in EPA-major (>=60% EPA) formulations and in patients concurrently taking antidepressants. Bleeding safety: Javaid et al., 'Bleeding Risk in Patients Receiving Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids', J Am Heart Assoc 2024 — 15 RCTs, 120,643 patients. I have corrected the previous version, which said this covered people on anticoagulants (the paper's analysis was of background antiplatelet therapy) and which omitted the paper's own high-dose purified EPA caveat. CAVEAT: this literature has high heterogeneity and probable publication bias, and effect sizes shrink in higher-quality trials — the recommendation reflects guideline consensus on how to dose it if you dose it, not certainty that it works.

protocols.bodyEffect: Vitamin D matters for bone, muscle strength and falls. What it does not reliably do is lift mood — the largest trial was flatly negative.
protocols.mechanism: Vitamin D receptors are present in brain regions involved in mood regulation, which is why the hypothesis was attractive — but the low vitamin D seen in depressed people is at least partly a consequence of being indoors and inactive rather than a cause of the depression.
doThis: Get tested before supplementing rather than guessing. Treating a real deficiency is worth doing; treating a normal level is not.
If you are deficient, correct it — for bone, muscle and fall prevention, which matters more than usual given the bone-density question with SSRIs and the dizziness some people get.
Typical maintenance dosing is 800-1000 IU per day. Higher is not better here.
Keep expectations calibrated: think of this as protecting your skeleton, not as treating your depression.
eatThis: Oily fish and egg yolks — modest amounts, but they overlap usefully with the omega-3 advice
Fortified milk, plant milks and breakfast cereals, which in many countries are the main dietary source
Sunlight on skin remains the dominant input for most people; food alone rarely covers it at higher latitudes in winter
avoidThis: Large intermittent bolus doses (the 50,000+ IU monthly or annual megadose approach) — trials of high intermittent dosing have found increased falls and fractures rather than fewer.

Believing marketing that presents vitamin D as an antidepressant. VITAL-DEP randomised 18,353 adults to 2000 IU/day of vitamin D3 or placebo over a median 5.3 years and found no effect on depression incidence and no effect on mood scores. That is about as clean a negative as this field produces.
protocols.timeline: Blood levels respond over 8-12 weeks of daily dosing; do not expect any mood change on any timescale
protocols.source: Okereke et al., 'Effect of Long-term Vitamin D3 Supplementation vs Placebo on Risk of Depression or Clinically Relevant Depressive Symptoms and on Change in Mood Scores' (VITAL-DEP), JAMA 2020;324(5):471-480 — 18,353 participants, 2000 IU/day D3, median 5.3 years, null for both incidence and mood scores. Supporting meta-analyses of vitamin D for depressive symptoms report high heterogeneity and publication bias and do not overturn this. The bone/muscle/falls rationale and the 800-1000 IU maintenance figure come from general bone-health guidelines, not from depression evidence — and note the tension with Massé et al., BMJ 2026, which found supplementation gave no clinically meaningful fracture benefit in community-dwelling adults; the case here is for correcting deficiency, not routine supplementation. The bolus-dosing harm signal comes from trials of high intermittent dosing (e.g. Sanders et al., JAMA 2010, annual 500,000 IU) and is a separate literature.

protocols.bodyEffect: Folate feeds the reaction that manufactures serotonin, dopamine and noradrenaline. Some people run that pathway less efficiently than others.
protocols.mechanism: L-methylfolate is the form of folate that crosses into the brain and donates a methyl group to regenerate tetrahydrobiopterin, the cofactor required by the enzymes that make all three monoamines — so if folate status is poor, the raw machinery your antidepressant depends on is under-supplied.
doThis: If you and your prescriber try it, use 15mg per day as an add-on to your existing antidepressant, for at least 8 weeks. That is the dose and design that produced the positive result; the 7.5mg arm did not separate from placebo.

Check B12 status first. Folate supplementation can correct the anaemia of B12 deficiency while the neurological damage continues underneath — this is established pharmacology, not a theoretical worry.
Get folate from food regardless, since it is cheap and the downside is nil.
Understand what you are buying. This is a plausible, modestly supported add-on for people who have not responded to an SSRI — not a first move, and not a correction of a genetic defect.
eatThis: Lentils, chickpeas and black beans — among the densest natural folate sources per serving
Dark leafy greens, especially raw or lightly cooked, since folate degrades with prolonged heat
Asparagus, avocado, and fortified breakfast cereals in countries that fortify
avoidThis: Using an MTHFR genotype result to decide whether to take it. In post-hoc analysis of the pivotal trials, MTHFR genotype did not significantly predict who responded — there was a non-significant trend toward greater benefit in C677T variant carriers, in a sample far too small to settle it. Either way there is currently no validated pharmacogenomic indication here, and MTHFR-guided methylfolate prescribing is not supported by the evidence that exists.
Using it as a standalone antidepressant. L-methylfolate has not been tested as monotherapy in a placebo-controlled trial, so nobody knows if it works alone.
protocols.timeline: The positive trial ran 60 days at 15mg/day; allow at least 8 weeks before judging
protocols.source: Papakostas et al., 'L-methylfolate as adjunctive therapy for SSRI-resistant major depression: results of two randomized, double-blind, parallel-sequential trials', Am J Psychiatry 2012;169(12):1267-74. HONEST READING: two sequential-parallel-comparison trials; the first (7.5mg) did not separate from placebo on its primary outcome, the second (15mg/day) did on both primary measures, with NNT for response approximately 6. One positive trial of modest size, industry-sponsored, not independently replicated at scale, never tested as monotherapy. The MTHFR analysis is exploratory and post-hoc in a small sample, showing no significant genotype prediction with a non-significant trend favouring variant carriers — this is absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence, but it is the only genotype evidence there is and it does not support genotype-guided prescribing. The B12-masking caution is long-standing established pharmacology.

protocols.bodyEffect: These raise serotonin by the same route as your medication or an adjacent one. Stacked on top, the total can tip over into serotonin syndrome.
protocols.mechanism: Your antidepressant blocks serotonin from being cleared out of the synapse; these supplements either add more reuptake blockade or pour in more raw material for making serotonin — and because the clearance route is already blocked, what would be a harmless amount on its own has nowhere to go.
doThis: Treat these four as prescription drugs, because pharmacologically they are: St John's Wort, 5-HTP, L-tryptophan, and SAMe. Tell your prescriber before starting any of them.

If you are on an MAOI (phenelzine, tranylcypromine), treat this as a different order of risk entirely, not a stronger version of the same one. With an MAOI the serotonin has no way out at all, and these combinations are contraindicated rather than cautioned.

Learn the picture of serotonin syndrome, because it comes on within hours of adding something, not days: agitation and restlessness, sweating, shivering, diarrhoea, fast heart rate, tremor, muscle twitching or jerking especially in the legs, overactive reflexes, fever, confusion. Twitchy plus sweaty plus agitated plus racing heart within hours of a new supplement means stop it and get seen the same day.
Check cough medicine. Dextromethorphan — the 'DM' in most over-the-counter cough syrups — is serotonergic and is the one almost nobody thinks of as a drug.
Read multi-ingredient 'mood support', 'calm' and 'sleep' blends ingredient by ingredient. 5-HTP and St John's Wort hide in these constantly.
avoidThis: St John's Wort — a double problem. It inhibits serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake itself, giving genuine additive serotonergic risk with documented serotonin syndrome case reports alongside sertraline and paroxetine. Separately, its hyperforin content is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 and of P-glycoprotein, which drops the blood levels of many other drugs — including hormonal contraceptives, where it has caused breakthrough bleeding and unintended pregnancy, and warfarin, ciclosporin and several antivirals.

5-HTP and L-tryptophan, which bypass the rate-limiting step in serotonin synthesis and deliver substrate straight into a system whose exit is already blocked. Tryptophan combined with serotonergic antidepressants is a classic serotonin syndrome setup.
SAMe, which has antidepressant-like activity of its own, has case reports of serotonin syndrome alongside SSRIs, and can precipitate mania in people with bipolar disorder.

Stopping St John's Wort abruptly without telling your prescriber if you have been on it. Removing the enzyme induction lets levels of your other medications climb, so the risk runs in both directions.
Recreational MDMA, and be aware that tramadol, linezolid and triptans are prescription items that also add serotonergic load — mention your antidepressant whenever any of these come up.
protocols.timeline: Serotonin syndrome typically begins within hours of adding the offending agent, usually inside 24 hours; St John's Wort enzyme induction takes roughly 1-2 weeks to build and a similar time to wear off
protocols.source: Serotonin syndrome interactions with St John's Wort, tryptophan, 5-HTP and SAMe appear as contraindications or warnings on serotonergic antidepressant labels; the MAOI combinations are contraindications. St John's Wort CYP3A4/CYP2C19 and P-gp induction via hyperforin, dose-dependent on hyperforin content: Borrelli & Izzo, 'St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum): drug interactions and clinical outcomes', and the European Psychiatry 2025 review of SJW-SSRI interactions documenting serotonin syndrome cases predominantly with sertraline and paroxetine. I have dropped CYP2C9 from the induction list — the evidence for it is weaker than for 3A4 and 2C19 — and added P-gp, which is well established. Contraceptive failure with SJW is a well-documented pharmacokinetic interaction. NOTE ON HONESTY: the triptan-SSRI serotonin syndrome warning derives from an FDA advisory based on sparse case reports and has been challenged by subsequent cohort data — it is deliberately included as 'mention it' rather than 'avoid it'. SAMe evidence is case reports only, which is weaker than the others listed here. The St John's Wort induction onset/offset timing is pharmacological convention rather than a precisely measured figure.

protocols.bodyEffect: Mirtazapine blocks the histamine and serotonin receptors that tell your brain you have eaten enough. Hunger returns after dinner, often aimed at carbs.
protocols.mechanism: Mirtazapine is a potent H1 histamine antagonist and 5-HT2C antagonist, and both receptors sit in the hypothalamic circuits that generate satiety, so the drug removes the 'stop eating' signal rather than adding a 'start eating' one.
doThis: Plan for it rather than resisting it. Make dinner your largest and most protein-heavy meal so the evening craving lands on a full stomach instead of an empty one.

Pre-portion an evening snack before you take the dose: something in the 200-300 kcal range with protein in it (Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, a boiled egg). Decide while you are alert, not while you are sedated and hungry.
Take the dose 1-2 hours after your evening meal, so peak sedation and peak appetite do not arrive while you are standing in front of an open fridge.
Weigh weekly from day one, same day and time. Appetite change on this drug shows up early, and you want a trend line rather than a memory.
eatThis: A substantial protein portion at dinner (chicken thigh, salmon fillet, 200g Greek yoghurt, tofu with lentils). Larger single-meal protein doses blunt later appetite more reliably than small ones.
Slow carbohydrate rather than none: oats, barley, beans, wholegrain toast. Giving the craving something to land on beats pretending it is not there.

High-volume, low-calorie bulk at the evening meal: vegetable soup, big salad, air-popped popcorn. H1 blockade blunts chemical fullness signalling, so physical stomach stretch is one of the few satiety signals still getting through.
avoidThis: Do not keep the craving foods within arm's reach of the bed or sofa. H1 blockade causes strong sedation as well as hunger, and choices made half-asleep are not really choices.
Do not cut carbohydrate to zero in the evening. The craving is a real receptor-level signal, and total restriction usually ends in a larger, less controlled binge.

Do not ask for a dose reduction on the assumption that lower doses cause less weight gain. The inverse dose-response for sedation is well described; the equivalent claim for weight is clinical lore rather than evidence, and undertreating your depression is the worse trade.
protocols.timeline: Appetite change often starts within the first week. Weight gain on this drug is front-loaded into the early months of treatment.
protocols.source: VERIFIED against mirtazapine US prescribing information (Remeron/DailyMed): increased appetite 17% vs 2% placebo; weight gain of 7% or more of body weight in 7.5% vs 0% placebo; 8% discontinued for weight gain in pooled premarketing US studies. The 8-week PEDIATRIC trial figure (49% gained 7% or more vs 5.7% placebo; mean +4 kg vs +1 kg) is also on the label but must be presented as pediatric — mirtazapine is not approved for pediatric use and these figures should NOT be shown to an adult as their expected outcome. Receptor pharmacology (high-affinity H1 and 5-HT2C antagonism) is well characterised. MECHANISTIC INFERENCE, stated plainly: that the craving is carbohydrate-selective and evening-weighted comes from 5-HT2C biology plus consistent patient report, not a controlled feeding trial. NONE of the doThis or eatThis items are label-derived; they are practical inference from the receptor mechanism.

protocols.bodyEffect: How much you gain in the first weeks predicts where you land later. This is the window where acting is cheapest.
protocols.mechanism: Drug-induced weight gain is front-loaded because appetite and satiety signalling shift almost immediately, and the eating pattern that follows becomes habit before it becomes fat mass, so the trajectory is set well before the weight shows up.
doThis: Record a baseline weight before or on day one, then weigh weekly under the same conditions. Do not weigh daily: normal fluctuation is 1-2 kg and daily numbers will only distress you.
Set a tripwire in advance. A 5% rise from your starting weight in the first month (about 3.5 kg if you started at 70 kg) is the trigger to raise it with your prescriber, not a reason to wait and see.
Start countermeasures in week one rather than waiting for something to correct. Structured non-drug intervention does produce measurable benefit in this setting, and starting early costs you nothing.
Separate the two causes honestly: if depression had suppressed your appetite, some early regain is recovery and is a good sign. Drug-driven gain is the part that continues past your old baseline.
avoidThis: Do not wait until your mood improves or your dose stabilises before paying attention to weight. By the time you feel well enough to care, most of the front-loaded window has already passed.
protocols.timeline: Baseline on day one. The checkpoints that matter are weeks 4, 8 and 12. In a mixed psychotropic cohort, more than 5% weight gain at one month was the best early predictor of 15% or more gain by three months.
protocols.source: CORRECTED ATTRIBUTION. The 5%-at-1-month figure is Vandenberghe et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2015;76(11):e1417-e1423 — 351 psychiatric patients followed 1 year at Lausanne. More than 5% gain at 1 month predicted 15% or more gain at 3 months (sensitivity 67%, specificity 88%) and 20% or more at 12 months (sensitivity 47%, specificity 89%). The previous version attributed this to 'antipsychotic literature' and caveated that it did not apply to antidepressants; that is wrong in BOTH directions — the PsyMetab-type cohort covers weight-inducing psychotropics including antipsychotics, mood stabilisers AND antidepressants such as mirtazapine. It is still not SSRI-specific. Supporting: Predicting antipsychotic-induced weight gain in first-episode psychosis, European Psychiatry 2023 (27 studies, 4426 participants) found trend of early BMI increase within 12 weeks to be the most clinically significant prognostic factor for long-term ANTIPSYCHOTIC-INDUCED WEIGHT GAIN prognosis specifically — not for long-term outcome generally, as previously worded. Intervention figure: BJPsych Bulletin, 'Evaluation of components of non-pharmacological interventions for weight management in early antipsychotic therapy', found -1.93 kg and -1.12 kg/m2 at 6 months. REMOVED: the claim that 'prevention consistently outperforms reversal'. That was a naive cross-study juxtaposition of the 1.93 kg prevention figure against the 1.5 kg reversal figure in different populations and designs; no head-to-head comparison exists.

protocols.bodyEffect: SSRIs are not one thing for weight. Paroxetine is the outlier; sertraline and fluoxetine sit nearer neutral. Same class, different drugs.
protocols.mechanism: Paroxetine carries meaningful anticholinergic (muscarinic) activity that its SSRI siblings largely lack, which is the most plausible reason it separates from them on weight despite sharing the serotonin-reuptake mechanism.
doThis: If weight matters to you, name it as a selection criterion before you start rather than after. It genuinely changes which drug is a sensible first pick.
If you are gaining on paroxetine, treat that as a possible drug-specific effect. Switching within the same class is a real option, and assuming 'all SSRIs will do this to me' is not supported.
Ask your prescriber to look at the individual drug data rather than class-level generalisations, and bring the specific comparison you care about.
avoidThis: Do not stop or switch paroxetine on your own. It has one of the shortest half-lives in the class and abrupt discontinuation produces a genuinely rough withdrawal syndrome.
protocols.timeline: The divergence between paroxetine and the rest emerges over months, not weeks. The trial that separated them ran 26-32 weeks.
protocols.source: NUMBERS CORRECTED. Fava et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2000;61:863-867: 284 patients randomised to fluoxetine, sertraline or paroxetine; 139 completed 26-32 weeks (fluoxetine 44, sertraline 48, paroxetine 47). VERIFIED from the abstract: paroxetine produced a significant weight increase, fluoxetine a modest NONsignificant decrease, sertraline a modest NONsignificant increase; significantly more paroxetine patients gained more than 7% of body weight (widely reported as 25.5% paroxetine vs 6.8% fluoxetine vs 4.2% sertraline). DELETED: the previously quoted mean changes of '-0.2% fluoxetine, +1.0% sertraline, +3.6% paroxetine'. Those figures do not appear in the source; secondary summaries of the same paper report -1.3%, +0.1% and +1.7%, and the +3.6% paroxetine figure is roughly double any sourced value. Directions are reported here without invented magnitudes, and note the ≥7% proportions are completer-only on ~45 patients per arm. VERIFIED: Petimar et al., Annals of Internal Medicine 2024 (target trial emulation, 183,118 adults, 8 US health systems), 6-month mean weight change vs sertraline: escitalopram +0.41 kg, paroxetine +0.37 kg, duloxetine +0.34 kg, venlafaxine +0.17 kg, citalopram +0.12 kg, fluoxetine -0.07 kg, bupropion -0.22 kg. HONEST NOTE TO PRESERVE IN UI: these two studies disagree on magnitude. The modern EHR study finds far smaller average differences than the older randomised data, and averages hide individual variation in both directions.

protocols.bodyEffect: Average weight change on most antidepressants is small. The risk is not a sudden gain, it is a slow drift that keeps going for years.
protocols.mechanism: Serotonergic drugs appear to tilt the body's defended weight slightly upward, and the effect behaves like a small persistent bias rather than a discrete event, which is why it only becomes visible over years.
doThis: Once past the first 12 weeks, switch from weekly to monthly weighing and keep doing it. A drift of 0.5 kg a month is invisible day to day and is 6 kg a year.
Treat years 2 and 3 as the window needing active attention. That is where the population risk signal peaks and it is exactly when most people have stopped paying attention.
Re-baseline once a year: compare against your weight at initiation, not against last month, because monthly comparisons will never show you the trend.
protocols.timeline: Risk of gaining 5% or more of body weight is elevated across long-term treatment and peaks around years 2 and 3 rather than at the start.
protocols.source: Gafoor, Booth & Gulliford, BMJ 2018;361:k1951. UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink, 294,719 participants (136,762 men, 157,957 women), 2004-2014. VERIFIED: adjusted rate ratio for 5% or greater weight gain 1.21 in antidepressant users versus non-users, with risk remaining elevated over long-term follow-up rather than being confined to the first months. The year-2 (1.46), year-3 (1.48), NNH 59 and mirtazapine (1.50) figures are commonly cited from this paper's tables but I could not re-verify them against the full text in this pass, so they are stated here directionally rather than as precise ratios — do not print the decimals in the UI without a full-text check. The mirtazapine-specific ratio has in any case been removed from this protocol, whose drug list does not include mirtazapine. LIMITATION: observational. Confounding by indication, and by appetite recovery as depression remits, cannot be fully excluded, so some of this signal is recovery rather than drug effect.

protocols.bodyEffect: Drug weight gain is fat gain, and dieting against it costs you muscle too. Lifting is what protects the muscle; cardio alone does not.
protocols.mechanism: Under an energy deficit the body breaks down muscle alongside fat unless muscle is given a mechanical reason to stay, and resistance training supplies that stimulus in a way steady-state cardio does not.
doThis: Two full-body resistance sessions per week is the effective minimum; three is better. For this specific problem, adding lifting is the higher-value addition.
Four to six compound movements per session: a squat or leg press, a hinge, a push, a pull, a carry. Two to three sets each, stopping one or two reps short of failure.
Start smaller than feels serious if you are depressed and unfit. Fifteen minutes of bodyweight work twice a week, sustained for six months, beats week-one intensity you abandon by week three.
Keep cardio, but for mood and cardiometabolic health rather than as your weight tool. Both matter and they do different jobs.
avoidThis: Do not diet hard without resistance training, especially on a sedating drug. The scale will move, a meaningful share of what you lose will be muscle, and lower lean mass means lower resting energy expenditure and easier regain.
protocols.timeline: Strength improves in roughly the first month, mostly neural adaptation. Visible body-composition change takes months. Expect the scale to lag or stall early while muscle is added as fat comes off.
protocols.source: DOWNGRADED from clinical_studies to mechanistic_inference. The underlying principle — that resistance training during energy restriction preserves fat-free mass better than caloric restriction alone or aerobic training alone — is consistently supported across body-composition meta-analyses in general overweight and obese populations. But I could not verify the specific 2022 systematic review previously cited here by its stated description, so no single trial or effect size is quoted. CRITICAL POPULATION GAP: no trial has tested resistance training specifically against mirtazapine-, olanzapine- or clozapine-induced weight gain. The muscle-preservation physiology is not drug-specific, so the extrapolation is reasonable, but this is inference applied to this population, not a demonstrated result in it. The specific set, rep and session prescriptions are conventional programming practice, not trial-derived doses. FIXED: previous version said 'six to eight compound movements' then listed five.

protocols.bodyEffect: Protein is the macronutrient that most reliably blunts appetite and protects muscle. On an appetite-raising drug, both of those matter more.
protocols.mechanism: Protein produces a strong and long-lasting satiety response per calorie, carries the highest thermic cost to digest, and supplies the amino acid signal that keeps muscle protein synthesis running while calories are restricted.
doThis: Target roughly 1.2-1.6g of protein per kg of body weight per day. At 70kg that is about 85-110g. Use the upper end if you are actively dieting and lifting.
Spread it across the day: a decent portion at each of three meals beats 15g, 15g and 70g at dinner, because both the appetite and the muscle-synthesis effects are per-meal rather than per-day.
Aim for a substantial protein breakfast, in the 25-35g range, if you are someone who skips breakfast. That is the meal most often missed and the one where added protein has been tested most directly.

Anchor to real amounts so you can hit the number without tracking: 3 eggs is about 18g, 200g Greek yoghurt about 20g, a chicken breast about 35g, 150g tofu about 17g, a whey scoop about 25g, 100g cooked lentils about 9g.
eatThis: Eggs, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, skyr. High protein per calorie and require essentially no cooking, which matters enormously when you are depressed.
Whey or soy protein powder if solid food is unappealing in the early weeks. It is food, not a supplement gimmick, and it is often the difference between hitting the target and not.
Tinned fish, tinned beans, frozen edamame, supermarket rotisserie chicken. Protein you can eat during a week when cooking is not going to happen.
protocols.timeline: You may feel the appetite effect at the very next meal. Effects on body composition take weeks to months and depend on total intake and training.
protocols.source: DOWNGRADED from clinical_studies — the trials are real but none were done in people taking these drugs. VERIFIED: Leidy et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2013 — randomised crossover, n=20 overweight/obese 'breakfast-skipping' late-adolescent girls; 350-kcal high-protein (35g, egg- and beef-rich) breakfast, but not a 350-kcal normal-protein (13g) breakfast, improved satiety and reduced evening snacking versus breakfast skipping, with corresponding changes in food-cue fMRI reward signal. That is one small pilot in a narrow population. SOFTENED: the previous claim that 'protein's appetite effect is most consistent at 30g or more' was stated as an established threshold. It is an extrapolation from a handful of small dose-comparison studies including this n=20 one; there is no validated 30g cut-off, so the copy now says 'larger single-meal doses' and gives a range. The 1.2-1.6 g/kg intake target and the higher 1.6-2.4 g/kg figure for energy restriction come from resistance-training and sports-nutrition literature in non-psychiatric populations. HONEST LIMIT TO KEEP IN UI: the NewStart randomised trial found no effect of high- versus low-protein breakfast on body composition in young women with overweight. Protein reliably helps hunger and muscle retention; on its own it is not a weight-loss intervention.

protocols.bodyEffect: If your hunger arrives at night, moving calories earlier means the evening craving meets a body that has already been fed.
protocols.mechanism: Drugs that drive evening appetite create a predictable daily shape, and matching intake to that shape means the craving arrives against existing fullness rather than a genuine accumulated deficit.
doThis: Do not skip breakfast on an evening-craving drug. Skipping breakfast to 'save' calories for the evening is the most reliable way to make the evening worse.
Try shifting more of your intake to breakfast and lunch for two weeks, and judge it on your own hunger rather than on the scale.
Keep a planned evening snack inside the budget rather than trying to eliminate it. Removing it entirely tends to backfire on a drug that is pharmacologically generating that hunger.
protocols.timeline: You can judge the effect on your hunger pattern within about two weeks. Any effect on weight, if it exists, takes months.
protocols.source: VERIFIED: Jakubowicz et al., Obesity 2013;21:2504-2512 — 93 overweight/obese women with metabolic syndrome, isocaloric ~1400 kcal/day for 12 weeks; big-breakfast group (700/500/200 kcal) lost about 8.1 kg versus about 3.3 kg in the big-dinner group (200/500/700 kcal), with greater reductions in fasting glucose, insulin and HOMA-IR. THERMIC-EFFECT FIGURES CORRECTED: Romon et al. 1993 reported TEF of 15.9% at 0900, 13.5% at 1700 and 10.9% at 0100 — the previous version said '16% vs 14% vs 11%', rounding 13.5 the wrong way. FURTHER CAVEAT ADDED: later work (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022) argues that circadian variation in resting metabolic rate largely accounts for the apparent daily rhythm in TEF, so even this small mechanism is contested. BE HONEST WITH USERS: this is one 93-person trial with an unusually large effect that has not replicated consistently, and the meal-timing literature is mixed, with several trials finding no advantage once total calories are matched. Present front-loading as a sensible way to manage a drug-driven hunger pattern, not as a proven weight-loss method. REMOVED: the specific '40/35/25' split, which was invented and is not the ratio used in any cited trial.

protocols.bodyEffect: Bupropion raises dopamine and noradrenaline signalling in appetite circuits. Food stops being interesting rather than making you feel full.
protocols.mechanism: Bupropion stimulates POMC neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus, increasing melanocortin satiety signalling, while raised dopaminergic tone lowers the reward value of food, so appetite drops from two directions at once.
doThis: Eat on a schedule rather than on appetite. If hunger is not arriving, hunger cannot be your cue, so set three fixed meal times and keep them regardless.
Make the calories you do eat count: protein-dense and fat-dense rather than large volumes of low-calorie food you will not finish.
Weigh weekly. Unintended loss is easy to miss when you also feel more energetic and clearer-headed, and those improvements can mask a deficit.
eatThis: Calorie-dense and low-effort: nut butters, full-fat yoghurt, olive oil added to everything, cheese, avocado.
Smoothies with oats, whole milk or soy milk, nut butter and protein powder. Liquid calories go down far more easily than solid food when appetite is genuinely absent.
avoidThis: Do not use bupropion's appetite suppression as a deliberate weight-loss tool without telling your prescriber that is what you are doing. It changes the risk calculation, particularly seizure risk at higher doses and in anyone restricting intake.
protocols.timeline: Appetite suppression usually appears within the first weeks and often persists rather than fading the way early nausea does.
protocols.source: VERIFIED: Petimar et al., Annals of Internal Medicine 2024 — bupropion -0.22 kg at 6 months versus sertraline and roughly 15% reduced risk of gaining 5% or more of baseline weight, the most favourable weight profile of the 8 first-line antidepressants studied. Gafoor et al., BMJ 2018 is consistent in direction. The POMC/melanocortin and dopaminergic-reward mechanism is established translational pharmacology and underpins bupropion's use in the naltrexone-bupropion obesity combination. MECHANISTIC INFERENCE: attributing any individual patient's appetite loss to that specific pathway is inference, not measurement. The '1-2 weeks' onset previously stated was not sourced and has been softened to 'within the first weeks'.

protocols.bodyEffect: Fluoxetine often causes modest early weight loss that does not last. Over a year it comes out roughly weight-neutral.
protocols.mechanism: Fluoxetine acutely reduces energy intake, but the effect attenuates with continued treatment, and weight then tends to recover as depression remits and appetite returns.
doThis: Do not build your eating habits around the early suppression. It is borrowed, not permanent, and the pattern you set in week three will meet a returning appetite months later.
If you are losing weight you did not intend to lose, add calories deliberately now rather than waiting to see whether it continues.

Expect the later months to feel like weight gain when much of it is the early loss reversing and depression lifting. Knowing that in advance stops it reading as personal failure and stops it triggering a stop-the-drug decision.
protocols.timeline: Loss is an early-weeks effect and is small. By a year of treatment fluoxetine is roughly weight-neutral.
protocols.source: NUMBERS CORRECTED AND STRENGTHENED. VERIFIED: Michelson et al., Am J Psychiatry 1999;156:1170 — 839 patients in a 12-week acute phase, 395 randomised to fluoxetine 20mg or placebo for up to 50 further weeks. Mean absolute weight DECREASE of 0.4 kg during the first 4 weeks across all patients; among 50-week completers, weight gain was similar on fluoxetine (about 3 kg) and placebo (about 3.2 kg), with the authors attributing the later gain to recovery from depression rather than to the drug. That placebo comparison is the strongest single fact in this protocol and was missing from the previous version. VERIFIED: Petimar et al., Annals 2024 — fluoxetine -0.07 kg (95% CI -0.19 to 0.04) versus sertraline at 6 months, statistically indistinguishable. DELETED: the '-0.2% on fluoxetine' figure previously attributed to Fava 2000; that number does not appear in the source, which reports only a modest nonsignificant decrease without a stated magnitude in the abstract. IMPORTANT: larger weight-loss figures circulating for fluoxetine (for example around 4.7 kg at 6 months) come from trials at 60 mg/day in overweight and obese populations, above typical antidepressant dosing, and must not be quoted to a patient on 20 mg for depression.

protocols.bodyEffect: Metabolic risk is drug-specific, not class-wide. Olanzapine and clozapine sit in a different category from aripiprazole or lurasidone.
protocols.mechanism: H1 and 5-HT2C blockade drives the appetite increase, but muscarinic M3 blockade separately impairs insulin secretion, which is why olanzapine and clozapine can damage glucose handling through a route that does not require weight gain to happen first.
doThis: Get fasting glucose or HbA1c plus a lipid panel at baseline, at 12 weeks, then at least annually. Watching the scale alone will not catch the glucose problem, because it can move independently.

Find out where your specific drug sits. Olanzapine and clozapine have the worst metabolic profiles; aripiprazole, brexpiprazole, cariprazine, lurasidone and ziprasidone the most benign. 'It is an antipsychotic' tells you almost nothing on its own.

If you are starting olanzapine or clozapine, ask about co-starting metformin at the same time rather than waiting. The 2025 Schizophrenia Bulletin guideline recommends co-commencement for high-risk agents, and metformin is the only drug shown to prevent this weight gain.

Note that the metformin guideline's own trigger is a 3% rise in body weight in the first 12 months — a lower bar than the 5%-at-one-month tripwire used elsewhere in this app. Take whichever fires first as your prompt to act.
Apply the resistance-training and protein protocols here with more urgency than for antidepressants. The magnitude of gain is larger and the cardiometabolic stakes are higher.
avoidThis: Do not reduce or stop an antipsychotic yourself over weight. Relapse risk dominates the calculation and any switch has to be planned and covered.
Do not assume a normal weight means normal metabolism on olanzapine or clozapine specifically. Insulin resistance has been demonstrated in non-obese patients on these two drugs.
protocols.timeline: Weight gain is fastest in the first 12 weeks. Glucose and lipid changes can appear early, and can appear before or without meaningful weight change.
protocols.source: VERIFIED AND STRENGTHENED. Pillinger et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2020, network meta-analysis of 18 antipsychotics: olanzapine and clozapine worst across weight, BMI, glucose and lipids; aripiprazole, brexpiprazole, cariprazine, lurasidone and ziprasidone most benign; risperidone and paliperidone produced weight gain without substantial fasting glucose increase, which is the cleanest single demonstration that these parameters dissociate. Huhn et al., Lancet 2019 (402 RCTs, 53,463 participants) ranks clozapine and olanzapine among the highest for clinically significant weight gain. VERIFIED: Carolan et al., 'Metformin for the Prevention of Antipsychotic-Induced Weight Gain: Guideline Development and Consensus Validation', Schizophrenia Bulletin 2025;51(5):1193 — AGREE II-developed guideline; metformin is the only pharmacological agent with demonstrated efficacy for preventing antipsychotic-induced weight gain, reducing gain by about 4.03 kg versus control when co-commenced; recommends co-commencement with olanzapine or clozapine, and with medium-risk agents (quetiapine, paliperidone, risperidone) where cardiometabolic risk factors, age 10-25, or BMI 25-30 are present. The previous version cited this guideline but omitted its actual recommendations and effect size.

protocols.bodyEffect: Losing weight can feel like a bonus. It stops being one when you are undereating protein, losing muscle, or feeding an eating disorder.
protocols.mechanism: Appetite suppression removes the signal that normally drives intake, so intake falls below need without any discomfort to warn you, and the resulting deficit comes disproportionately out of lean mass when protein is low and resistance training is absent.
doThis: Set a floor rather than a target: a weight below which you contact your prescriber. Decide the number now, while you feel neutral about it, not later when you may not want to.
Protect protein first. If total intake is falling, protein should be the last thing cut, not the first thing crowded out.

If you have any history of anorexia, bulimia or binge-eating disorder, say so explicitly before starting bupropion. It is contraindicated in current or prior bulimia and anorexia nervosa because of elevated seizure risk. This is the one hard rule on this page.
Watch the quiet signals rather than the scale: hair shedding, feeling cold all the time, losing strength you previously had, periods becoming irregular or stopping.
eatThis: Fixed anchor meals that require no appetite and no decision: overnight oats with protein powder, a smoothie, cheese and crackers, nut butter on toast.
avoidThis: Do not let appetite suppression become the real reason you want to stay on a drug. If it is working for your mood, good. If the weight effect is the main appeal, that is worth saying out loud to your clinician rather than managing privately.
protocols.timeline: Watch the first three months most closely. That is when suppression is strongest and when unintended loss accumulates without being noticed.
protocols.source: DOWNGRADED from 'label' because the label content covers only ONE of the four listed drugs. VERIFIED label fact: bupropion US prescribing information contraindicates use in patients with a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia or anorexia nervosa, due to a higher observed incidence of seizures in such patients. There is no equivalent label statement for fluoxetine, venlafaxine or duloxetine, and the previous evidenceStrength of 'label' implied there was. IMPORTANT ADDITION: fluoxetine is the opposite case — it is FDA-approved for bulimia nervosa (60 mg/day), so it must not be presented alongside the bupropion eating-disorder contraindication in a way that implies a shared warning. MECHANISTIC INFERENCE: the lean-mass, thermoregulatory and menstrual consequences of sustained undereating described here are general nutrition physiology, not antidepressant-specific trial findings, and the listed warning signs are clinical judgement rather than validated thresholds. The personal weight floor is a practical safeguard, not an evidence-based cut-off.

protocols.bodyEffect: Switching off a weight-gaining drug does not automatically return you to your old weight. Some comes off; a lot often stays.
protocols.mechanism: Stopping the drug removes the appetite driver, but the accumulated fat mass and the eating patterns learned around months of altered hunger persist independently, so you reverse the cause without reversing the effect.
doThis: Expect partial reversal and plan for it. In antipsychotic trials, dose reduction, discontinuation, or switching specifically to a partial agonist produced about 1.5 kg of loss versus staying put: real, but small next to what people typically gained.

Use the switch window deliberately. Appetite drops once the pharmacological driver is removed, and that is the easiest opportunity you will get to rebuild eating patterns. Do it then rather than 'once things settle'.
Keep resistance training running through the switch, so that what you lose is fat rather than the muscle you built.
If weight is your main reason for switching, ask specifically about moving to bupropion or sertraline rather than switching blind, since the individual-drug differences are what matter here.
avoidThis: Do not switch on weight grounds alone if the current drug is working well for your mood. Relapse costs more than the kilograms, and a failed switch can be hard to walk back.

Do not stop the current drug yourself while waiting for a switch to be arranged. Discontinuation syndromes are worst on short-half-life drugs like paroxetine and venlafaxine, and an unplanned gap is the commonest way a switch goes badly.
protocols.timeline: Appetite typically normalises within weeks of removing the driver. Weight loss, where it happens, is gradual over months and is usually partial rather than complete.
protocols.source: VERIFIED: Speyer et al., 'Reversibility of Antipsychotic-Induced Weight Gain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis', Frontiers in Endocrinology 2021 — 40 RCTs and 15 uncontrolled studies, 12,279 individuals. Dose reduction, drug discontinuation, or switch TO A PARTIAL AGONIST reduced weight by 1.5 kg (95% CI -2.03 to -0.98) versus maintenance; uncontrolled pre-post change was -1.13 kg. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the previous version's action step said 'dose reduction, discontinuation or switching' and dropped 'to a partial agonist', which implied any switch delivers this benefit. It does not — the pooled estimate is specific to that comparator set. The authors themselves note few studies were designed with this as a primary outcome. HONEST GAP: direct evidence on reversal after ANTIDEPRESSANT-induced weight gain is thin. 'Expect partial reversal' is extrapolated from the antipsychotic literature plus general weight-regain physiology and should be presented as a reasonable expectation, not a measured result.

protocols.bodyEffect: Melatonin is cleared by the same enzyme fluvoxamine blocks, so a standard supplement dose can act like a much larger one.
protocols.mechanism: Melatonin is metabolised principally by CYP1A2; with fluvoxamine blocking that enzyme, melatonin exposure rose roughly 17-fold in a small healthy-volunteer study.
doThis: Do not add a melatonin supplement while on fluvoxamine without asking your prescriber first. This is not a small interaction.

If you already take melatonin and have just started fluvoxamine, expect heavy morning grogginess and vivid dreams. Raise it rather than pushing through and concluding the antidepressant is intolerable.

For sleep in the first weeks, use a fixed wake time and 10-15 minutes of outdoor morning light instead. Neither goes through CYP1A2, and both shift your own melatonin timing rather than adding to a pool you cannot clear.
avoidThis: Melatonin-containing 'sleep gummies' and combination sleep supplements, which often do not lead with melatonin on the front of the pack.
protocols.timeline: The effect is present from the first days of fluvoxamine and lasts the whole course.
protocols.source: Härtter et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2000 (PMID 10668847): 5 healthy male volunteers given 5mg oral melatonin with or without a single 50mg fluvoxamine dose; melatonin AUC approximately 17-fold higher and Cmax approximately 12-fold higher. Very small, single-dose, healthy-volunteer design — the direction is solid, the exact multiple in a real patient on steady-state fluvoxamine is not established. Caffeine also competes at CYP1A2 and can raise melatonin exposure on its own, so the two plausibly stack; direction only, no reliable multiplier.

protocols.bodyEffect: Cigarette smoke revs up the enzyme that clears these drugs. Stop smoking and clearance falls within days, so the same dose becomes a bigger dose.
protocols.mechanism: It is the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in smoke, not the nicotine, that induce CYP1A2. Induction fades over days from the last cigarette and reaches a new steady state in about a week, while your prescription stays where it was.
doThis: Tell your prescriber before your quit date, not after. This is a dose conversation, not a willpower conversation.
Expect the change over roughly the first week after quitting: more sedation, nausea, unsteadiness, a drugged or slowed feeling. That is a level rise, not the quit going badly.
On clozapine or olanzapine, ask specifically about a planned reduction plus blood-level monitoring. Australian Prescriber suggests daily reductions of about 10% until the fourth day after cessation.
Cut your coffee down when you quit too. Caffeine runs through the same CYP1A2, so part of the jitteriness and insomnia of quit week is caffeine levels rising, not only nicotine withdrawal.

Do not skip this because you are using patches, gum or a vape. Nicotine replacement therapy does not influence CYP1A2, so it does not hold the enzyme up. Switching to NRT counts as quitting, metabolically.
avoidThis: Assuming a slow cigarette taper is metabolically gentle. As few as 7-12 cigarettes a day is enough for close to maximal induction, so most of the enzyme change happens in your last few cigarettes.

Assuming smoked cannabis is different. Combustion products rather than the cannabinoid are the inducer — but note this specific point is mechanistic inference from the tobacco data, not separately measured for cannabis.
protocols.timeline: Caffeine clearance falls about 36% on cessation of heavy smoking, reaching a new steady state at roughly one week (about 8 days). On clozapine or olanzapine the clinical consequences may take longer to become obvious.
protocols.source: Australian Prescriber, 'Smoking and drug interactions' (verified directly): 'A 50% difference in the mean daily dose of clozapine needed by smokers and nonsmokers to reach a given blood concentration has been reported'; 'a mean increase of 72% in plasma clozapine concentrations' after cessation; 'a new steady state of CYP1A2 activity reached after approximately one week'; 'Nicotine replacement therapy does not influence CYP1A2 activity'; 'daily dose reductions (of approximately 10% until the fourth day after smoking cessation)'. Time course: Faber & Fuhr, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004 — 12 heavy smokers, caffeine clearance fell 36.1% (95% CI 30.9-42.2%) to a new steady state after cessation. 7-12 cigarettes/day sufficing for near-maximal induction: Oxford Health and Tees/Esk NHS formulary guidance. Case reports in CYP1A2-genotyped patients: PMID 16044115.

protocols.bodyEffect: Starting or increasing smoking speeds up clearance of these drugs, so a dose that was working can quietly stop working.
protocols.mechanism: The same PAH-driven CYP1A2 induction, running the other direction. Smokers carry substantially lower steady-state levels of duloxetine, fluvoxamine and mirtazapine on identical doses.
doThis: If your smoking has gone up during a bad stretch and the medicine feels like it has stopped working, say both things in the same sentence. 'It pooped out' and 'I am on 20 a day now' can be one event, not two.
Note roughly how much you smoke whenever a dose is set, so there is a baseline to compare against later.

Know where this is least likely to be your explanation. Escitalopram, citalopram and bupropion showed no significant smoking effect in the systematic review, so on those a loss of effect needs a different explanation and this should not distract from finding it.
Do not read this as a reason to keep smoking. It is a reason to change the dose deliberately rather than accidentally.
avoidThis: Silently self-adjusting your dose to compensate. The level change is real but the right size of correction needs measurement, especially for clozapine and olanzapine.
protocols.timeline: Induction builds over roughly a week of regular smoking and reverses over roughly a week after stopping.
protocols.source: Systematic review of smoking and antidepressant pharmacokinetics (PMC5340025), verified directly: nonsmokers had about 43% higher steady-state duloxetine concentrations than smokers; fluvoxamine serum levels significantly higher in nonsmokers (reductions exceeding 30% in smokers); S-mirtazapine and R-N-desmethylmirtazapine significantly lower in smokers; venlafaxine parent showed no significant difference but ODV metabolite was 21% lower in smokers. CORRECTION TO PRIOR DRAFT: sertraline is MIXED, not clean — one study found significantly lower concentration-to-dose ratios in smokers, another found no significant correlation. Fluoxetine parent showed no correlation but norfluoxetine was higher in smokers. Only escitalopram, citalopram and bupropion were clean negatives. Duloxetine labelling notes smoking reduces bioavailability by roughly a third. TDM cohort: PMID 30192450.

protocols.bodyEffect: Grapefruit destroys CYP3A4 in your gut wall, so more of each dose survives absorption and the dose in the pill stops matching the dose reaching you.
protocols.mechanism: Furanocoumarins in grapefruit irreversibly inactivate CYP3A4 inside intestinal cells. The gut has to build new enzyme, which is why a single glass matters for days and why the effect is on first-pass absorption rather than on liver clearance.
doThis: Treat one 200-250mL glass as enough to matter. This is not a dose-response you can drink around by having less.

If grapefruit genuinely matters to you, keep it constant rather than occasional, and tell your prescriber, so the dose gets set against your actual diet. An unpredictably inhibited enzyme is harder to prescribe against than a consistently inhibited one.
Do not bother spacing grapefruit a few hours from your dose. The enzyme is destroyed, not temporarily occupied, so timing does not rescue it.
Watch for the real-world signal: more side effect on an unchanged dose within a day of the juice. Sedation, dizziness, nausea, dry mouth.
Allow a few days after your last grapefruit before assuming you are back to baseline, since the gut has to synthesise new enzyme.
eatThis: Ordinary oranges, mandarins, satsumas, lemons and limes — they do not carry the relevant furanocoumarins and are fine.
Standard or blood orange juice as a direct substitute if what you want is the citrus and the vitamin C.
avoidThis: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice, pomelo, tangelo, and Seville (bitter) orange including marmalade made from it — all carry furanocoumarins.
Multi-fruit and 'breakfast blend' juices without reading the label, since grapefruit is a common component not flagged on the front.
protocols.timeline: Intestinal CYP3A4 protein falls within about 4 hours of a glass. Recovery requires synthesis of new enzyme and takes on the order of one to three days.
protocols.source: Buspirone: Lilja et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 1998 (PMID 9871430) — grapefruit juice raised mean buspirone Cmax 4.3-fold (range 2 to 15.6) and AUC 9.2-fold (range 3 to 20.4). NOTE: the 4.3-fold figure is Cmax, not AUC; a prior draft presented it as the headline exposure change and understated the AUC effect. Sertraline: Lee et al., Clin Ther 1999 (PMID 10890261) — n=5 patients on stable sertraline, trough rose from 13.7 to 20.2 µg/L (+47%) after one week of 240mL grapefruit juice daily. Real but very small; sertraline also has a wide safety margin, so this is 'worth knowing' not 'alarm'. Enzyme kinetics: the ~47% fall in enterocyte CYP3A4 within 4 hours is Schmiedlin-Ren et al., Drug Metab Dispos 1997, in a SINGLE volunteer — it was misattributed to Lown et al., J Clin Invest 1997 in a prior draft; Lown found a 62% fall in 10 men after 6 days. The commonly quoted '50% recovery at 24h, full at 72h' could not be traced to a primary source and has been removed. Negative: clozapine and haloperidol showed no significant grapefruit interaction (PMC12437050).

protocols.bodyEffect: For these three the grapefruit effect is predicted from enzyme pathways, not measured. The direction is likely; the size is unknown.
protocols.mechanism: All three are cleared substantially by CYP3A4, and grapefruit inactivates intestinal CYP3A4 — so an exposure rise is expected. But no one has given grapefruit alongside these drugs and measured what happens.
doThis: Treat this as a reason to mention grapefruit to your prescriber, not a reason to panic about a glass you already drank.
If you are on quetiapine, the caution is strongest: the label instructs reducing the dose to one sixth with a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, which tells you how much headroom this pathway has.

If you are on vilazodone, note that its absorption is unusually food-dependent in the first place — taking it fasted drops AUC by about 50% and Cmax by about 60% versus fed. Taking it consistently with food matters more than grapefruit does.
Judge by symptoms rather than by theory: more sedation, dizziness or dry mouth on an unchanged dose within a day of grapefruit is the signal worth reporting.
avoidThis: Regular daily grapefruit alongside quetiapine specifically, given the size of the ketoconazole effect and the label's dose-reduction instruction.
protocols.timeline: If present, the effect would follow the same course as other grapefruit interactions — onset within hours, unwinding over a few days.
protocols.source: Quetiapine: no human grapefruit PK study exists. The Seroquel label reports ketoconazole increased quetiapine AUC 5- to 8-fold and directs reducing the dose to one sixth with a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor (Grimm et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2006 measured ~6-fold). Extrapolating from a potent azole to grapefruit overstates grapefruit, which is a moderate intestinal inhibitor — treat the direction as real and the magnitude as much smaller and unquantified. Vilazodone: VERIFIED — the word 'grapefruit' does NOT appear anywhere in the FDA vilazodone label (DailyMed setid c3e167cd-7f56-45eb-80df-a60fa1392e57). The label says only 'The vilazodone hydrochloride dose should not exceed 20 mg once daily with the concomitant use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor.' Secondary sources that state 'grapefruit caps vilazodone at 20mg' are extrapolating and should not be presented as label text. Food effect verified verbatim: 'Vilazodone AUC and Cmax in the fasted state can be decreased by approximately 50% and 60%, respectively, compared to the fed state.' Trazodone: CYP3A4 substrate, no human grapefruit study located.

protocols.bodyEffect: Alcohol and these drugs press the same sedative brakes in the brain, so the impairment adds up even though your blood alcohol does not change.
protocols.mechanism: Alcohol potentiates GABA-A inhibition and blocks NMDA excitation. Mirtazapine, trazodone, quetiapine and the tricyclics add histamine H1 and alpha-1 blockade on top. The effect is additive at the receptor, which is why 'avoid alcohol' is about how you function, not about drug levels.
doThis: If you are going to drink, do it once you know how the medicine affects you. Not in the first two weeks, and not in the week after a dose increase.
Halve what you would normally have and check how you actually feel before the second drink. Judge from your body now, not from your old tolerance.
Do not drive after any alcohol on a sedating antidepressant. The additive impairment is the specific thing that catches people out.

Watch the mood cost, not just the sedation. Alcohol fragments the second half of the night and suppresses REM, so it directly undoes the sleep repair the medicine is trying to deliver — relief tonight and a worse tomorrow.
Be honest about amount as well as frequency when you are asked. Most intake questions record how often and miss how much.
avoidThis: Alcohol in the evening alongside mirtazapine, trazodone or quetiapine. All three are strongly sedating and this combination is the most common source of 'I cannot function the next morning on this'.
Using alcohol to get through the first weeks of side effects. It makes exactly those weeks worse, for the sleep reason above.
protocols.timeline: Additive sedation is there from the first dose and is worst in the first two weeks and after each increase. Sedation commonly eases over subsequent weeks, though this is clinical expectation rather than a measured trajectory.
protocols.source: US antidepressant labels in this class carry either an explicit advisory against alcohol or a somnolence/impairment precaution covering driving and operating machinery; the specific wording varies by product and should be checked per drug before display rather than asserted as uniform. The receptor pharmacology (ethanol potentiation of GABA-A and NMDA antagonism; H1 and alpha-1 blockade by mirtazapine, trazodone, quetiapine and TCAs) is established pharmacology, not a trial result. Stated honestly: most antidepressants do not measurably change blood alcohol concentration, and the size of the additive impairment is a clinical rule of thumb with no measured multiplier — never display it as a number.

protocols.bodyEffect: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold, and alcohol lowers it further on the way down. The risk sits in the withdrawal, not in the drinking.
protocols.mechanism: Bupropion is dose-dependently pro-convulsant. Alcohol raises the seizure threshold while it is on board and rebounds below baseline as it clears, so the dangerous moment is abruptly stopping a heavy or daily drinking pattern, not the drink itself.
doThis: Keep alcohol low and, above all, steady. Steadiness matters more here than the average amount.
If you want to stop drinking and you drink daily or heavily, plan it with your prescriber. Supervised withdrawal, not a cold-turkey weekend.
Avoid a binge pattern of heavy nights and dry days. The swing is the risk, not the mean intake.
Tell your prescriber about anything else lowering the threshold at the same time: skipped meals, poor sleep, stimulants, tramadol, benzodiazepine withdrawal.
avoidThis: Abruptly stopping heavy or daily alcohol use while taking bupropion.
Bupropion at all with current or past anorexia nervosa or bulimia — a label contraindication.
protocols.timeline: Alcohol-withdrawal seizures classically cluster roughly 6 to 48 hours after the last drink. That window is from the alcohol-withdrawal literature, not from the bupropion label.
protocols.source: Bupropion US label: contraindicated in patients undergoing abrupt discontinuation of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates or antiepileptic drugs; contraindicated in patients with a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia or anorexia nervosa; seizure risk is dose-dependent and stated in the label; label advises minimising or avoiding alcohol. The 6-48 hour withdrawal-seizure window is standard alcohol-withdrawal teaching and is not a bupropion-label figure — a prior draft implied it came from the label.

protocols.bodyEffect: Duloxetine can injure the liver by one route and heavy drinking injures it by another, leaving less reserve to absorb either.
protocols.mechanism: Duloxetine can cause idiosyncratic hepatocellular injury. Chronic alcohol separately induces CYP2E1, which generates oxidative stress and depletes glutathione — so the liver has less spare capacity when a second insult arrives.
doThis: Be specific about how much you drink, not just how often. The standard intake question captures frequency and misses volume, and volume is what matters here.
Ask for baseline liver tests before starting if you drink regularly.
Get urgent review for yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, pain under the right ribs, unusual itching, or unexplained deep fatigue.
Be careful with paracetamol/acetaminophen too. It runs through the same CYP2E1 route to a toxic metabolite, and it is the most common thing people quietly add for the headaches of the first weeks.
avoidThis: Heavy or chronic alcohol use alongside duloxetine. The label is specific about this combination, which is stronger than the generic 'avoid alcohol' on other antidepressants.
protocols.timeline: Idiosyncratic liver injury is unpredictable in timing rather than dose-related, so this is a watch-for-symptoms risk across the whole course rather than a first-fortnight one.
protocols.source: Duloxetine US label, hepatotoxicity warning, verified wording: Cymbalta 'should ordinarily not be prescribed to patients with substantial alcohol use or evidence of chronic liver disease' because duloxetine and alcohol may interact to cause liver injury or duloxetine may aggravate pre-existing liver disease. DILI Network case series: PMC3773985. CYP2E1 induction by chronic ethanol and its role in oxidative hepatic stress and glutathione depletion is established (Lu & Cederbaum). Stated honestly: that the two mechanisms compound quantitatively is mechanistic inference — the label warning is real, the additive size is not measured.

protocols.bodyEffect: St John's Wort speeds up the enzymes clearing your antidepressant and adds serotonin of its own, so it can weaken and overshoot at the same time.
protocols.mechanism: Hyperforin is a potent ligand for the pregnane X receptor, which switches on CYP3A4 transcription — the same route prescription enzyme inducers use. Separately, St John's Wort inhibits monoamine reuptake, so it adds serotonergic load while lowering the level of the prescribed drug.
doThis: Do not start St John's Wort alongside a prescribed antidepressant without telling your prescriber. Of everything sold over the counter, this is the one that most changes your pharmacology.
If you are already on it, do not stop it abruptly on your own either. Induction unwinds over one to two weeks and your antidepressant level will climb as it does — a planned stop, not a silent one.
Tell your prescriber the brand and the dose. Induction tracks hyperforin content, which varies widely between products, so 'St John's Wort' is not a single exposure.

Know the serotonin-excess picture if you are on both: agitation, sweating, shivering, tremor, jumpy or twitchy reflexes, diarrhoea, fast heartbeat, fever. Several of those together is an emergency, not a side effect to sit with.
Remember what else it strips through the same enzyme: hormonal contraception, anticoagulants, some HIV, transplant and cancer drugs. The contraception failure route is the one people miss.
avoidThis: Combining it with an SSRI, SNRI, vortioxetine, vilazodone, a triptan or tramadol without supervision.
Treating it as 'natural, therefore additive-free'. Mechanistically it behaves like a prescription enzyme inducer with an antidepressant bolted on.
protocols.timeline: Induction builds over roughly 10 to 14 days of daily use and takes a similar one to two weeks to unwind after stopping.
protocols.source: Hohmann et al., Clin Transl Sci 2024 (PMC11329750), verified directly: dose-dependent CYP3A induction measured with oral midazolam microdoses after 14 days at 300, 900 and 1800 mg/day, giving estimated metabolic clearance increases of 1.96-fold (95% CI 1.66-2.31), 3.86-fold (3.39-4.40) and 5.62-fold (4.82-6.56) respectively. TWO FIGURES REMOVED from a prior draft: the '52% fall in mean substrate AUC' at 900mg and the hyperforin-content correlation 'R = 0.87, p = 0.004' do not appear in this paper; the authors report fold-changes in clearance and note qualitatively that induction correlates with hyperforin but not hypericin content, without giving that coefficient. Moore et al., PNAS 2000: hyperforin activates PXR and induces CYP3A4 in primary human hepatocytes (the specific Ki was not re-verified and is omitted). Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs rests on case reports and regulator advisories (Medsafe NZ 2012) rather than trials — real but not trial-quantified.

protocols.bodyEffect: These drugs can make you hold onto water, diluting the sodium in your blood. Drinking more plain water makes that worse, not better.
protocols.mechanism: SSRIs and SNRIs can trigger inappropriate ADH release (SIADH), so the kidney retains free water. Sodium is not being lost so much as diluted — which is why the instinctive fix, drinking more, is the wrong direction.
doThis: Know the symptoms, because they impersonate both depression and a bad start on the drug: headache, poor concentration, memory trouble, confusion, weakness, unsteadiness, feeling generally muddled. Falls or a seizure are the severe end.
If those appear in the first few weeks, ask for a sodium blood test rather than assuming the drug 'is not agreeing with you'. It is a specific, measurable thing.
Know if you carry the risk factors: older age, low body weight, a thiazide or other diuretic, vomiting or diarrhoea, or a previous episode of low sodium.
Drink to thirst. Do not deliberately push fluids to 'flush out' side effects or to fix a headache — with SIADH, extra free water lowers sodium further.
Do not stop the drug on your own if you suspect this. Get the sodium measured and let your prescriber decide, because abrupt stops carry their own problems.
avoidThis: Loading up on plain water, electrolyte-free squash or large volumes of tea in response to headache or grogginess in the first weeks.
Starting an SSRI/SNRI and a new diuretic in the same window without a plan to check sodium.
protocols.timeline: Most reported cases occur within the first few weeks of starting or of a dose increase, which is exactly when people are most likely to misread the symptoms as the depression or as normal early side effects.
protocols.source: US SSRI and SNRI labels carry a Hyponatremia warning describing cases of hyponatraemia and SIADH, identifying elderly, volume-depleted and diuretic-treated patients as higher risk, and advising consideration of discontinuation in symptomatic patients. FLAG FOR THE OWNER: this protocol was NOT in the set submitted for review — the review brief referred to 'the hyponatraemia fluid advice' as if it existed, and it does not. I have written a corrected version because the failure mode here is dangerous in the specific direction the brief was worried about (advising fluids). Before shipping, verify the warning section wording against each individual product label rather than treating it as uniform, and confirm whether any existing content elsewhere in the app tells users to increase fluid intake.

protocols.bodyEffect: Cannabis pulls two ways: CBD blocks several clearing enzymes and raises drug levels, while smoking anything induces CYP1A2 and lowers them.
protocols.mechanism: CBD inhibits CYP3A4/5, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP2B6 and CYP1A2 in laboratory systems. Independently, the combustion products of smoked cannabis are expected to induce CYP1A2 as tobacco smoke does, regardless of cannabinoid content. Which effect dominates depends on route and dose.
doThis: Tell your prescriber you use cannabis, and say which form. High-dose CBD oil and smoked flower are different pharmacology, not different amounts of the same thing.
If you change route — smoking to edibles or vaping, or the reverse — treat it as a smoking-status change for any CYP1A2 drug, and reread the smoking-cessation guidance.
Be most careful with high-dose CBD products alongside a narrow-margin drug: clozapine, a tricyclic, or anything where your level is already monitored.

Check the actual milligrams on CBD products. Over-the-counter doses vary enormously, and most of the interaction data comes from pharmaceutical epilepsy-scale CBD doses well above typical supplement use.
avoidThis: Assuming CBD is inert because it is not intoxicating. It is a broad multi-enzyme inhibitor in vitro, and that is precisely the property that makes interaction plausible.
Adding a high-dose CBD product on top of clozapine or a tricyclic without telling anyone.
protocols.timeline: CBD's enzyme inhibition would track use day to day. CYP1A2 induction from smoking follows the same roughly one-week on and one-week off course as tobacco.
protocols.source: Largely in vitro and in silico: Drug Metab Dispos 2024 (PMC11022895) on cannabinoid metabolites as CYP inhibitors; Front Psychiatry 2022 review of cannabinoid hepatic metabolism; reviews reporting time-dependent reversible inhibition of CYP2D6 and CYP1A2 and irreversible inhibition of CYP3A4 by CBD. Stated honestly and prominently: clinical antidepressant-specific interaction data is thin, and the human data that exists comes from pharmaceutical epilepsy-dose CBD. Treat the DIRECTION as likely and the MAGNITUDE as unknown — do not display numbers to users for this one. The smoked-cannabis CYP1A2 point is inference from tobacco data, not separately measured for cannabis.
